body: **Opt-in includes default-on configuration** When a flag or configuration enables new behavior by default, this definition classifies it as `opt-in` merely because configuration exists, allowing a changed unconfigured run to become auto-merge eligible even though the adjacent rule requires it to be classified as `new-default`. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!
